o1.biggest_strength: Honest, traceable forecast with a stated reach assumption, a 1,500 to 3,400 range, a per-topic table, and a short list of facts to confirm. The three new articles are in the brand voice and answer in the first lines.
o1.biggest_mistake: It writes new articles beside the old ones instead of fixing the 38%-helpful 'How balances work', so the old article stays unhelpful and two similar articles now compete. It also applies one 58% help rate to every topic, including Pro refunds, where the help rate is not the right measure.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the existing balances article instead of adding a duplicate, and size each topic's saving on its own cause (for example, Apple and Google refunds avoided) rather than one blended help rate.

o2.biggest_strength: It rewrites and renames the existing articles, which is the cheapest route to the ticket savings. Each topic is sized separately in a table. It also adds an in-app 'Balances are simplified. Why?' line, search-term tagging, and a currency link.
o2.biggest_mistake: The forecast shares (40%, 50%) are asserted with little evidence and look optimistic, so the headline 21% drop is probably too high. The website steps ('Undelete expense', 'Recent activity') and the Apple and Google cancel paths are invented details, and the 'Contact us' form option is assumed.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tie the avoidance shares to the existing help rates or give a low-to-high range up front, and flag the invented UI names as needing a check.

reason: As the owner, I would rather have the one that rewrites my weakest, biggest article, retitles the delete article in my customers' words, and adds the in-app 'Balances are simplified. Why?' idea. Its forecast is rosier and some details are invented, but it works through each topic, whereas Output 1 is safer and more honest on the numbers but adds duplicate articles.
